questiontext.text:
UniCV prototype for test-table questions in Python (based on python3_test_table, with a new interface and a new grader). The student completes a table of tests for a function or a program described in the question: the test code (or the standard input) and the exact output it should produce. Each test is run with the teacher's reference solution; a row is valid when the solution prints exactly the expected output. Optionally, the student's tests must also catch some wrong versions of the code, so that the student has to think of the important cases.

How to write a question

  1. In the Question text, describe the function or program to be tested (e.g. is_even(number) returns True if the number is even) and ask the student to complete the table.
  2. Open Answer preload and build the table there: choose whether the tests are Python code that calls a function or the standard input of a program, add the rows and write the cells. Cells with text are given; leave a cell empty for the student to fill in, or write ??? in it for the parts the student must complete (e.g. print(is_even(???))). You can also let students add some tests of their own.
  3. Save (Save changes and continue editing). The table now appears in the Answer field: fill in the open cells correctly, and write the reference solution in the box below the table.
  4. Optionally, add wrong versions after the reference solution, each starting with a line #### wrong: description. The description is shown to the student when their tests do not catch that mistake.
  5. Keep Validate on save ticked: the teacher's answer must be valid (and catch every wrong version). No test cases are needed, and Twig all is not needed.

Example of reference solution with two wrong versions:

def is_even(number):
    return number % 2 == 0
#### wrong: does not work for negative numbers
def is_even(number):
    return number > 0 and number % 2 == 0
#### wrong: says that 0 is odd
def is_even(number):
    return number != 0 and number % 2 == 0

What the student gets

  • A table with numbered rows: the given cells in grey, the cells to fill in white, and for ??? cells a reminder of the part to complete. The cells grow as the student types.
  • A counter of the cells filled in, a Help panel, a Start again button (with confirmation) and, if allowed, Add a test to add tests of their own.
  • After Check, each of the student's rows is marked ✓ or ✗ with the reason (empty cell, ??? not replaced, the test is not in the required form, the test gives an error, or the expected output is not what the test prints). If all tests are valid but some wrong version is not caught, the student is told which mistakes their tests miss.

Grading

  • With All-or-nothing grading (the default), the mark is 1 only if all the student's rows are valid and all the wrong versions are caught.
  • Otherwise the mark is the fraction of the student's rows that are valid, multiplied by the fraction of wrong versions caught.
  • Only the student's own tests (rows whose test cell the student wrote) count for catching wrong versions. A wrong version is caught when one of those tests prints something different, or gives an error, with it.

Limitations

  • The output is compared exactly, line by line (spaces at the end of lines are ignored).
  • For function tests, each test is run on its own after the reference solution, so the test code must print what it checks (e.g. print(is_even(4))).
  • The given cells always come from the Answer preload: if a student changes them in the page, the grader ignores those changes. If the table is changed after students have answered, their answers are matched row by row.
  • The reference solution and the wrong versions are stored in the teacher's Answer, which students do not see during the quiz (but, as with any question, it is shown in the review if Right answer is enabled).

Differences from python3_test_table

  • New interface: the table is built in the Answer preload with buttons (add, move and delete rows), and the Answer shows the same table plus the reference solution. There is no need to copy serialised data with Ctrl+Alt+M.
  • Tests for programs (standard input and output), not only for functions.
  • Wrong versions that the student's tests must catch, a new way to assess the quality of the tests.
  • Students can add tests of their own, and each row is marked ✓ or ✗ in the table with the reason.
  • New self-contained grader: no support files and no pylint, a time limit per test (endless loops are reported) and clear messages.

Note on input(): for program tests, by default input() behaves as on the keyboard: the prompt and the value read (followed by a new line) appear in the output, so they must be in the expected output. For example, with a = int(input("a? ")) and input 3 the output starts with a? 3. Set echostandardinput to false to get plain Python behaviour.

Template parameters (all optional)

  • testre (default ""): a regular expression that every test written by the student must contain (searched with re.DOTALL). Explain the required form in the question text. Example: {"testre": "print\\(is_even\\(-?\\d+\\)\\)"}.
  • showexpected (default false): if true, when an expected output is wrong the student is shown what the test really prints (useful for practice, not for tests).
  • echostandardinput (default true): see the note on input() above.
  • timeout (default 3): time limit in seconds for each test.
  • strictwhitespace (default true): if false, differences in spaces inside lines are ignored.
  • proscribedbuiltins (default ["exec", "eval", "open", "compile"]): built-in functions the tests cannot use.
  • maxoutputlength (default 10000): longer outputs are cut.

Note: Moodle's emoticon filter turns some short texts in brackets, such as the letters n, y or i between round brackets, into icons in the question text. Avoid one-letter parameter names in the text of your questions (write is_even(number), not is_even with the parameter n), or turn off the emoticon filter for the course.

"""Grader for the UniCV test-table prototype (unicv_python3_test_table). The student completes a table of tests for a function (or a program) that the question author has written. Each row is a test: the test code (or the standard input, for a program) and the output that test should produce. The table, and which of its cells the student must fill, come from the question's Answer preload. The reference solution, and optionally some wrong versions of it, come from the question's Answer (the teacher's answer), so students never see them. A row is valid when running its test with the reference solution prints exactly the expected output written in the row. The student's own tests must also catch every wrong version: at least one of them must give a different result with it. Each row's result is written in the feedback as message, which the interface uses to mark that row. """ import builtins import html import io import json import re import signal import sys import traceback STUDENT_ANSWER = """{{ STUDENT_ANSWER | e('py') }}""" QUESTION_ANSWER = """{{ QUESTION.answer | e('py') }}""" QUESTION_PRELOAD = """{{ QUESTION.answerpreload | e('py') }}""" ALL_OR_NOTHING = "{{ QUESTION.allornothing }}" == "1" IS_PRECHECK = "{{ IS_PRECHECK }}" == "1" try: PARAMS = json.loads("""{{ QUESTION.parameters | json_encode | e('py') }}""") except ValueError: PARAMS = {} if not isinstance(PARAMS, dict): # Twig encodes an empty set of parameters as [] PARAMS = {} TESTRE = PARAMS.get('testre', '') SHOW_EXPECTED = PARAMS.get('showexpected', False) ECHO_INPUT = PARAMS.get('echostandardinput', True) TIMEOUT = float(PARAMS.get('timeout', 3)) MAX_OUTPUT = int(PARAMS.get('maxoutputlength', 10000)) STRICT_WHITESPACE = PARAMS.get('strictwhitespace', True) PROSCRIBED_BUILTINS = PARAMS.get('proscribedbuiltins', ['exec', 'eval', 'open', 'compile']) WRONG_MARKER = re.compile(r'^####\s*wrong\s*:?\s*(.*)$', re.I | re.M) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Reading the table # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def read_table(answer): """The table stored in an answer or in the preload, as a dict (empty if none).""" try: data = json.loads(answer) raw = data.get('table', ['']) raw = raw[0] if isinstance(raw, list) else raw table = json.loads(raw) if raw else {} return table if isinstance(table, dict) else {} except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError): return {} def cell(rows, i, j): try: return str(rows[i][j]) except (IndexError, TypeError, KeyError): return '' def is_open(text): """True if a cell of the preload is for the student (empty, or with ??? to complete).""" return text.strip() == '' or '???' in text def pattern_for(text): """A regular expression for a preload cell with ??? parts.""" return '^' + re.escape(text.strip()).replace(re.escape('???'), '.+') + '$' def split_solution(code): """The reference solution and the list of (description, code) wrong versions.""" parts = WRONG_MARKER.split(code) reference = parts[0] wrongs = [] for k in range(1, len(parts), 2): description = parts[k].strip() or f'wrong version {len(wrongs) + 1}' wrongs.append((description, parts[k + 1])) return reference, wrongs # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Running code # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- class TimeLimit(Exception): pass class OutOfInput(Exception): pass def on_alarm(signum, frame): raise TimeLimit() def forbidden(name): def stub(*args, **kwargs): raise NameError(f"'{name}' cannot be used in this question") return stub def run(code, testcode='', stdin=''): """Run the code and then the test code; return (output, error message or '').""" out = io.StringIO() names = dict(vars(builtins)) def echo_input(prompt=''): out.write(str(prompt)) line = sys.stdin.readline() if not line: raise OutOfInput() line = line.rstrip('\n') if ECHO_INPUT: out.write(line + '\n') return line def to_out(*values, sep=' ', end='\n', file=None, flush=False): out.write((sep if sep is not None else ' ').join(str(v) for v in values) + (end if end is not None else '\n')) names['input'] = echo_input names['print'] = to_out for name in PROSCRIBED_BUILTINS: names[name] = forbidden(name) scope = {'__name__': '__main__', '__builtins__': names} error = '' saved = sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr = io.StringIO(stdin), out, out signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, on_alarm) signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, TIMEOUT) try: exec(compile(code, 'solution.py', 'exec'), scope) if testcode.strip(): exec(compile(testcode, 'test', 'exec'), scope) except TimeLimit: error = 'the test takes too long (endless loop?)' except OutOfInput: error = 'input() was called but there is no more input data' except SystemExit: pass except SyntaxError as err: where = 'the test' if err.filename == 'test' else 'the solution' error = f'syntax error in {where}: {err.msg}' except BaseException: kind, value, tb = sys.exc_info() error = traceback.format_exception_only(kind, value)[-1].strip() finally: signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0) sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr = saved text = out.getvalue() if len(text) > MAX_OUTPUT: text = text[:MAX_OUTPUT] + '\n*** Output too long: cut ***\n' return text, error def normalise(text): lines = [line.rstrip() for line in text.replace('\r\n', '\n').rstrip().split('\n')] if not STRICT_WHITESPACE: lines = [' '.join(line.split()) for line in lines] return '\n'.join(lines).strip('\n') # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Grading # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def row_marker(i, ok, message): return (f'' f'{html.escape(message)}') def pre(text): return f'
{html.escape(text)}
' def main(): preload = read_table(QUESTION_PRELOAD) answer = read_table(STUDENT_ANSWER) teacher = read_table(QUESTION_ANSWER) program = preload.get('kind') == 'program' given_rows = preload.get('rows', []) extra_allowed = int(preload.get('addrows', 0) or 0) student_rows = answer.get('rows', []) solution_code = teacher.get('solution', '') or answer.get('solution', '') outcome = {'fraction': 0.0} if not solution_code.strip(): outcome['prologuehtml'] = ("

This question has no reference solution

" "

The teacher must write it in the Answer, in the box Reference solution. " "Please tell your teacher.

") return outcome reference, wrongs = split_solution(solution_code) # The rows to grade: the preload's cells where they are given, the student's where they are open, # then the rows the student added (at most extra_allowed, and not empty). rows = [] # (test, expected, test is the student's, expected is the student's, test pattern) index = [] # The position of each graded row in the student's table. for i, given in enumerate(given_rows): t0, e0 = cell(given_rows, i, 0), cell(given_rows, i, 1) t = cell(student_rows, i, 0) if is_open(t0) else t0 e = cell(student_rows, i, 1) if is_open(e0) else e0 rows.append((t, e, is_open(t0), is_open(e0), pattern_for(t0) if '???' in t0 else '')) index.append(i) added = 0 for i in range(len(given_rows), len(student_rows)): t, e = cell(student_rows, i, 0), cell(student_rows, i, 1) if not t.strip() and not e.strip(): continue added += 1 if added > extra_allowed: break rows.append((t, e, True, True, '')) index.append(i) test_name = 'input' if program else 'test' results = [] # (ok, message) problems = 0 for i, (t, e, t_mine, e_mine, pattern) in enumerate(rows): if (t_mine and not t.strip() and not program) or (e_mine and not e.strip()): results.append((False, 'Fill in this row.')) continue if (t_mine and '???' in t) or (e_mine and '???' in e): results.append((False, 'Replace the ??? in this row.')) continue if t_mine and pattern and not re.search(pattern, t.strip(), re.S): results.append((False, f'Only the ??? parts of the {test_name} may be changed.')) continue if t_mine and TESTRE and not program and not re.search(TESTRE, t, re.S): results.append((False, 'This test is not in the form asked for in the question.')) continue if program: got, error = run(reference, '', t if t.endswith('\n') else t + '\n') else: got, error = run(reference, t) if error: results.append((False, f'Running this {test_name} gives an error: {error}')) elif normalise(got) == normalise(e): results.append((True, 'Valid test')) else: message = 'The expected output is not what this test prints.' if SHOW_EXPECTED: message += ' It prints:\n' + got.rstrip('\n') results.append((False, message)) mine = [k for k, r in enumerate(rows) if r[2] or r[3]] valid_mine = [k for k in mine if results[k][0]] problems = len(mine) - len(valid_mine) # The wrong versions that the student's tests do not catch. missed = [] own_tests = [k for k, r in enumerate(rows) if r[2] and results[k][0]] if wrongs and not problems: for description, code in wrongs: caught = False for k in own_tests: t = rows[k][0] if program: got, error = run(code, '', t if t.endswith('\n') else t + '\n') else: got, error = run(code, t) if error or normalise(got) != normalise(rows[k][1]): caught = True break if not caught: missed.append(description) if IS_PRECHECK: outcome['fraction'] = 1.0 if not problems else 0.0 elif not mine: outcome['fraction'] = 1.0 else: valid_part = len(valid_mine) / len(mine) caught_part = 1.0 if not wrongs or problems else (len(wrongs) - len(missed)) / len(wrongs) if ALL_OR_NOTHING: outcome['fraction'] = 1.0 if not problems and not missed else 0.0 else: outcome['fraction'] = valid_part * caught_part # Feedback: a summary, the table of results and the markers for the interface. head = 'Input' if program else 'Test' parts = [] if not problems and not missed: parts.append("

All your tests are valid.

") if wrongs: parts.append(f'

They also catch all the {len(wrongs)} wrong version{"s" if len(wrongs) > 1 else ""} of the code.

') parts.append('
') elif problems: what = f'{problems} of your {len(mine)} tests' if len(mine) > 1 else 'Your test' verb = 'is' if problems == 1 else 'are' parts.append(f"

{what} {verb} not valid

" "

The rows marked \u2717 need to be corrected.

") else: parts.append("

Your tests are valid, but not enough

" "

Your tests do not catch these mistakes, which a wrong program could make. Add or change tests so that " "at least one of them would give a different result:

    ") parts.extend(f'
  • {html.escape(d)}
    • ' for d in missed) parts.append('
') if added < extra_allowed: free = extra_allowed - added parts.append(f"

You can still add {free} test{'s' if free > 1 else ''} of your own with Add a test.

") parts.append('
') style = 'style="border:1px solid #c4cdd5;padding:4px 8px;vertical-align:top"' parts.append(f'' f'') for k, ((t, e, t_mine, e_mine, _), (ok, message)) in enumerate(zip(rows, results)): if not (t_mine or e_mine): mark = '' else: mark = '\u2713' if ok else \ f'\u2717 {html.escape(message.splitlines()[0])}' parts.append(f'') parts.append('
#{head}Expected output
{index[k] + 1}{pre(t)}{pre(e)}{mark}
') for k, ((t, e, t_mine, e_mine, _), (ok, message)) in enumerate(zip(rows, results)): if t_mine or e_mine: parts.append(row_marker(index[k], ok, message)) outcome['prologuehtml'] = ''.join(parts) return outcome print(json.dumps(main()))
